class: Any decision-support wording guard (ADR-003) written as its own exact-substring list inside each module lets word-stem and spacing variants of banned advice through, and the separate lists drift apart, so the same banned sentence passes in one module and fails in another.
mechanism: Each builder wrote a fresh list of exact phrases ('guaranteed', 'recommended trade', 'risk-free', 'you should'); the scans compared lowercased substrings without normalising spaces or stems.

first_seen.where: W-024 backend/ofo/errors/model.py @ edfc6f0 (second list after W-005 backend/ofo/strategy/wording.py)
first_seen.evidence: Independent verifier: 'We guarantee returns', 'We recommend buying calls', 'Risk free setup', 'A sure-shot trade', 'Traders should hedge now.', 'You  should buy' (double space), 'This will reduce your losses' all ACCEPTED; W-005's verifier earlier found 'limited risk' on a naked call and a unicode-hyphen position word passing its own list.

occurrences.evidence: W-005 round-3 verifier: 'limited risk' on a naked call and unicode-hyphen words passed (deferred #10)

fix: One shared checker, backend/ofo/wording.py (normalise case, whitespace, invisible characters; stem-based patterns with word boundaries; list cites ADR-003), used by every module that emits user-facing text (W-024 fix round; W-005's wording.py delegates to it; W-020 told to use it).

detection.note: Becomes guarded when W-024's shared checker merges with the verifier's variant cases as tests; a follow-up check could assert no module other than ofo/wording.py defines a banned-phrase list (AST scan).
